item.title: Local Businesses Honored at Green Business Certification Awards
item.description: Several Santa Monica businesses earned recognition for their environmental leadership at the Green Business Certification Awards held January 16th at the Santa Monica Family YMCA, celebrating their commitment to sustainable practices and rigorous environmental standards.

item.title: Toxic Pesticide Remains in Widespread Use Across California Despite 2005 Phaseout Recommendation
item.description: Twenty years after officials recommended phasing out methyl bromide, the toxic pesticide remains widespread in California. New UCLA research shows some communities face exposure nearly double state safety recommendations, with port areas like Long Beach at highest risk.

item.title: Former Teacher Opens Community-Focused Gym on Pico Boulevard
item.description: Spry Fitness, a new appointment-only gym at 2222 Pico Blvd. in Santa Monica, offers personalized training in a non-intimidating environment. Owner Evan Spry, a former history teacher and local resident, designed the studio to welcome clients ages 12 to 80+.

item.title: Santa Monica approves new rules for who can work in businesses on City-owned property
item.description: The Santa Monica City Council voted 6-1 to adopt new worker recall and retention protections for hospitality businesses on the city-owned pier, requiring employers to rehire laid-off workers and retain existing staff for 90 days after ownership changes.

item.title: Student Involved in Low-Speed Collision with Waymo Autonomous Vehicle Near Santa Monica School
item.description: A student was involved in a low-speed collision with an autonomous vehicle near Grant Elementary School on last week, though no injuries were reported, according to Santa Monica police.The incident occurred at approximately 7:40 a.m. near 24th Street and Pearl Street, adjacent to the school campus. item.title: City Opens Applications for Cannabis Retail Licenses
item.description: Applications are now open for cannabis retailers in Santa Monica with a first-come, first-served process. The program includes a social equity component and a 4% cannabis business tax that was approved by 66% of Santa Monica voters in 2022.

item.title: Lawmaker Proposes Guaranteed Access to Human Customer Service
item.description: Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur introduced the Right to Human Customer Service Act requiring large California businesses to provide human customer service within five minutes. The bill aims to end situations where consumers are trapped in automated systems.

item.title: Around Town: DineLA, Leonard Cohen Tribute Concert, & Grammy Events
item.description: SMDP's weekly guide highlights Santa Monica's vibrant scene with DineLA Restaurant Week's final days, the Leonard Cohen tribute at Broadstage, Venice's food-replica workshops, and Grammy events in Los Angeles through February 6.
